translation_notes: TST = Namespace('http://example.com/test#') -> @prefix tst: <http://example.com/test#> . and TST.alink -> tst:alink; that is the whole notational change, and it is exact
the pattern argument of graph.triples((None, tst:alink, None)) shows the prefixed-name island working in ordinary Python operand position (inside a tuple, after a comma) with no syntactic friction
'from rdflib import Graph, Namespace' is kept verbatim although Namespace becomes unused on the ldpy side (only import lines may be adjusted, and only for executability)

nuance carried over from the full source file (outside the region): TST is also used there as a runtime object -- nsm.bind('tst', TST) and getattr(TST, 'col_pattern_%s_%s' % ...) -- which @prefix alone cannot supply, so a whole-file translation would have to keep the Namespace binding as well as the declaration

context shim: 'from context import Session, A, B' added (import line only). Running the region for real needs a live OpenLink Virtuoso server plus SQLAlchemy, sqla_rdfbridge and nose; context.py supplies in-memory stand-ins for the session, the two declarative classes and the TestMapping instance, materialising the rows as the quad map would (tst:tB/1 tst:alink tst:tA/1). The stand-ins are imported identically by both sides, and the region's own assertion still discriminates the translated term (renaming tst:alink makes the ldpy side raise AssertionError)
